activity_overrides.reason: Roberts's pirate company was highly mobile across the Atlantic. ATLAS therefore does not assign the mobile company a static homeland. This Activity-level representative anchor uses the well-attested West African theatre, including Sierra Leone and Ouidah, while explicitly not asserting that the full 1719-1722 itinerary remained in one subregion.
source_refs: Dictionary of Welsh Biography — Bartholomew Roberts: records operations and shore visits including Sierra Leone and his final campaign off West Africa
Royal Museums Greenwich — Death of Bartholomew Roberts: documents the 1721-1722 West African campaign, Ouidah, and the pursuit ending near Cape Lopez

activity_overrides.reason: Every's pirate company ranged from Europe through the Indian Ocean and later dispersed in the Caribbean, so a static polity homeland would be misleading. The representative Activity anchor is the career-defining 1695 capture of the Mughal Ganj-i-Sawai as it neared Surat; this is a display anchor, not a claim that the entire 1694-1696 itinerary stayed in northwest South Asia.
source_refs: World History Encyclopedia — Henry Every: records Indian Ocean and Red Sea piracy and the 1695 Ganj-i-Sawai capture near the coast of Surat
World History Encyclopedia — Henry Every timeline: records the May 1694 takeover and April 1696 dispersal
